context.problem_statement: Compute a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the sample mean of the provided dataset using the percentile method. Steps: (1) compute the observed sample mean, (2) perform 10,000 bootstrap iterations: in each iteration, sample N values with replacement and compute the bootstrap mean, (3) compute the 95% CI as the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap distribution, (4) also compute the BCa (Bias-Corrected and accelerated) bootstrap CI for comparison, (5) compare to the theoretical t-distribution CI and report whether they agree (within 5% relative difference). Report bootstrap standard error and bias estimate.
context.expert_knowledge: Bootstrap CI percentile method: np.percentile(boot_means, [2.5, 97.5]). BCa corrects for bias and skewness in the bootstrap distribution. Bootstrap SE = std(boot_means). Bias = mean(boot_means) - observed_mean. Theoretical t-CI: mean ± t_crit * (std/sqrt(n)) where t_crit = scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=n-1). Bootstrap and t-CI should agree closely for approximately normal data.
